tip.title: B2 Proficiency Tip
tip.text: For the Aptis B2 level, examiners look for collocations and idiomatic expressions related to learning. Instead of just saying "learn something," try "acquire a new skill" or "pursue academic excellence."

tip.title: Pro-Tip: Precision Matters
tip.text: While these words are synonyms, they carry different nuances. Use "Crucial" for high-stakes situations, and "Essential" for necessary components of a process.

tip.title: Academic Pro-Tip
tip.text: In formal writing, we often use "were" instead of "was" for all subjects in the if clause.

sections.title: Education Grammar Selection
sections.description: Refine grammatical precision and advanced writing skills.

questions.prompt: "If the government ________ more in vocational training, the skills gap would narrow significantly."
questions.explanation: Would narrow marks a hypothetical result, so the if-clause takes the past form invested; would invest is not used in this clause.

questions.prompt: "I wish I ________ more opportunities to acquire specialized knowledge during my undergraduate years."
questions.explanation: The speaker regrets a past lack of opportunities, so wish is followed by had; have and am having refer to present possession.

tip.title: Sentence Upgrade
tip.text: Original: "The course is very difficult. I want more teachers to help me." Upgrade: "This academic discipline is exceptionally challenging, and it would be highly beneficial if more tutors were available to support the learners."

sections.title: Education Practice: Vocabulary
sections.description: Choose the most appropriate academic term to complete the sentences.

questions.prompt: "At this university, Biology is treated as an academic _________, alongside Chemistry and Physics, rather than as a single school subject."
questions.explanation: An academic discipline is an established branch of knowledge. A curriculum is a programme, and a qualification is an award.

questions.prompt: "To be accepted into the Master's program, candidates must _________ all the entry requirements."
questions.explanation: Meet the requirements is the standard collocation meaning satisfy every stated condition; get and fill do not carry that meaning here.

questions.prompt: "Many professionals choose _________ learning because they can study while working full-time."
questions.explanation: Distance learning is the fixed term for study away from a campus; far learning and remote learning are not the target collocation.

questions.prompt: "Internships provide an excellent opportunity for students to _________ practical skills before graduating."
questions.explanation: Acquire skills means gain them through learning or experience; collect and hold do not express development of ability.

questions.prompt: "Places are limited, so make sure to _________ in the advanced grammar course before the registration deadline."
questions.explanation: Enroll in a course means officially join it. Register normally takes for here, while attend describes participation after joining.

questions.prompt: "The company highly values employees who demonstrate a commitment to continuous professional _________."
questions.explanation: Continuous professional development is the established workplace term; growing and advancing do not complete this noun phrase.

tip.title: Academic Tip
tip.text: In academic English, "discipline" is often used as a more formal synonym for "field of study" or "subject."

sections.title: Listening: Why Retrieval Practice Works
sections.description: Listen to a mini lecture and distinguish the main claim from supporting evidence.

audio.transcript: Students often assume that rereading is the safest way to remember new material. It feels productive because the text becomes familiar. Familiarity, however, is not the same as being able to retrieve an idea when the book is closed. Retrieval practice asks learners to bring information to mind through a quiz, a flashcard or a short written summary. The effort involved strengthens access to that knowledge. This does not mean that every lesson should become a test. Low-stakes retrieval works best when mistakes are followed by clear feedback and when questions are revisited after increasing intervals. Research also suggests that mixing related topics can improve discrimination: students learn not only how to apply a method, but when it is appropriate. There is one important caution. If learners retrieve an incorrect answer repeatedly without correction, the error may become stronger. Effective retrieval practice therefore combines effort, spacing and timely feedback. The wider lesson is that learning should sometimes feel difficult. A strategy that feels fluent during study may produce weaker memory later, whereas a challenging activity can create more durable understanding.

gistQuestions.prompt: What is the lecture's central argument?
options: Effortful retrieval with feedback improves durable learning
All learning should be formally tested
gistQuestions.explanation: The lecture supports retrieval combined with spacing and feedback.

options: Familiarity can be mistaken for recall
detailQuestions.explanation: A familiar text does not guarantee the learner can retrieve its ideas.

detailQuestions.prompt: What risk does the lecturer identify?
options: Repeated incorrect retrieval may strengthen an error
detailQuestions.explanation: Uncorrected wrong answers can become more firmly learned.

tip.title: Listening Tip
tip.text: Separate the thesis, mechanisms, conditions and caution; these are common mini-lecture signposts.

sections.title: Education Practice: Writing Part 4
sections.description: Write a short formal response using the vocabulary learned.

prompt.situation: You are attending an English course for Master's preparation. However, the study materials are outdated. Write a short message (30-50 words) to the center using "I wish..." or "If I were..." and the vocabulary learned.
prompt.referenceAnswer: I wish the study materials were more up to date. If I were responsible for the course, I would provide more academic resources and practical guidance to help learners acquire the skills they need.

tip.title: B2 Writing Tip
tip.text: To achieve higher marks in the Writing component, elevate your tone by using sophisticated adverbs to qualify your adjectives, such as highly beneficial or extremely challenging.
